title: Savoy Approves TP&L Rate Hike; Dr. Shaw Purchases Medical Clinic
text:
Savoy Approves TP&L Rate Hike;
Dr. Shaw Purchases Medical Clinic

By EULA PHILLIPS
Savoy Correspondent

SAVOY — A Texas Power and Light Co. rate hike and Dr. John Shaw's agreement to purchase the Savoy Medical Center were top items discussed in a City Council meeting this week.

Councilmen approved a 6.80 percent rate increase for TP&L, as recommended by the Public Utilities Commission in Austin. The increase is effective with the July billing.

H.F. Bomar, trustee for the Savoy Memorial Medical Center Association, appeared before the Council to explain the status of the clinic. Bomar gave the council a copy of the Articles of Association which are now on file at the City Hall.

The Association was founded in November, 1961, a board of trustees consisting of 10 persons were nominated, and only two of those members are still living. They are Harry F. Bomar and Holly Doan.

Bomar, who now lives in McKinney and Doan, who has retired from public work, chose to dissolve the Association as provided for under the Articles of Association.

The By-laws stipulate that after Dr. Shaw has paid a sufficient amount of rent to repay the cost of building the clinic, he was to be given the option to buy the building.

The second alternative in the event Dr. Shaw failed to exercise his option, was to give the building to the city and to divide any funds or monies the Association had on hand with the four churches of Savoy.

Dr. Shaw opened the clinic in July, 1961, and has been the only doctor here for 17 years.

Vernon Mullican, owner of the Mullican Nursing Home, appealed his sewer rates as being too high and asked for relief on his rates. He stated that his water and sewer bill costs $600 per month and he feels entitled to a lower rate. He was advised that the rate has been approved by the State, and the present rate structure is necessary to meet bond requirements, and at this time, no rate reduction can be put into effect.

The Council voted to nullify the action taken by the Board of Equalization which met April 17th, 1978. This action was taken because of the protest of citizens.

Status Of Savoy Medical Clinic Subject Of Study By City Dads

p[?]-7-8[?]

SAVOY — Who really owns the Savoy Medical Clinic?

This is a subject the city fathers pondered at length last night without arriving at any conclusion.

Councilmen Tommy Melugin and Billy Wrenn said they had tried to reach Harry Bomar, who was city bookkeeper at the time the clinic was built.

Melugin said there were no available city council minutes that showed how the clinic was to be operated. He said it was generally understood that Dr. John Shaw had the first chance at buying it.

Melugin said last September the medical board who owns the building, wanted to give the clinic to the city now that it has been paid out. However, it was understood that Dr. Shaw had 90 days to decide whether or not to personally buy it. He is paying $100 monthly rent.

No word has been heard from Dr. Shaw, and the 90 days has long since passed. It was indicated at last night's meeting that Bomar lived in McKinney and he was asked and he wrote and asked him to appear at last night's meeting.

"We wanted him to explain the status of the clinic, but he didn't show," Melugin said.

As a result, Melugin said he would write the secretary of state and try and get the articles of incorporation to find out the clinic's status.
